01 · What changes

Current · example

One release boundary

The illustrative service enables access for its entire audience at once.

Proposed

An explicit audience

The release owner chooses a pilot or all users. Both paths require a tested access switch.

Unchanged

Existing data ownership

This example changes access to a feature, not ownership of user data.

Keep the discussion beside the decision

A smaller audience limits initial exposure. It also adds recruitment work and can miss uncommon workflows.

A broad release reaches everyone immediately. A failure affects more people before the team disables access.

02 · The proposed boundary

Decision tree · Q1

  1. Pilot group

    Recruit participants → verify workflow coverage → review expansion.

  2. All users

    Verify recovery readiness → release broadly → review support reports.

  3. Unsure or unanswered

    Check recruitment and coverage. Hold the audience decision; continue recovery tests.

How to explain a score or estimate

04 · Perspectives and the current call

These authoring slots are not completed reviews. Choose a fast, single-author role-play or actual independent reviewers for a real unresolved decision.

For role-play, label this section and every card “Simulated perspective · single author.” For independent review, attribute only contributions actually received.

Advocate · unassigned

The strongest case

Choose a roster character. Show its portrait, name, role, and provenance. State the case, evidence, cost, and condition where this option fits.

Judge · unassigned

The deciding evidence

Name the evaluation criterion, result, and observable fact that would change the result.

Decision owner · unassigned

The proposed next step

Separate the owner's recommendation from the reviewer's response. Record release gates and what remains open.

Make the disagreement useful

Give each option equal space. Challenge the strongest rival argument and answer its objection. Question the premise when needed.

Assess correctness, simplicity, and user value. State what evidence would change each assessment. Preserve uncertainty and dissent.

Independent agents can challenge assumptions shared by a single author's role-play. Use them when the decision warrants the extra time.

A roster portrait is not approval. Simulated voices are not independent reviews, real participant messages, or live presence. Never invent endorsements or consensus.

05 · Delivery and proof

  1. 1 · Independent check

    Test recovery

    Owner: assign before work.

    Done when: disabling access blocks new entry and leaves existing data readable.

  2. 2 · Depends on Q1

    Prepare the audience

    Owner: release owner.

    Done when: the selected audience and required workflows are recorded.

  3. 3 · Depends on 1 + 2

    Review release readiness

    Owner: assign before work.

    Done when: the owner reviews recovery evidence and explicitly authorizes release.

Risks and exclusions

Disabling access cannot undo prior writes. Data migration and automatic rollback are outside this example's scope.

Authoring a plan that supports annotation layers

Keep section IDs stable across revisions. Give each section a meaningful heading. These anchors let people and agents refer to the same passage at different screen sizes.

The host supplies the avatar dropdown, live overlays, and agent tools. Do not duplicate that navbar or put collaboration credentials in this document. A connected agent should read the document and its annotation layers together.

For a historical export, identify the exact document version and annotation checkpoint heads. Preserve note IDs, author attribution, target sections, resolved state, and missing-content warnings. Do not imply this embedded example contains every live contribution.

Keep the copy response available. Direct submission requires a host-supported request channel with a delivery acknowledgement; an online portrait alone is not proof that an agent received the request.
